newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 12.0/13.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 12.0/13.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 12.0/13.0 percent on Friday on sufficient liquidity.
Dealers said overnight money rose to a high of 17 percent before easing as operators were engaged in arbitrage with the swap market, which was swamped by offshore players.
They said longer-term rates also swung, with one-week money rising to 17.0 percent before cooling off to 14.0 percent.
One-month money settled at 15.5 percent from 18.0 percent.
Dealers said an early central bank supply of 550 billion rupiah sufficed to cover weekly tax payments due Friday.
The central bank kept its bilateral rates unchanged, with one-week bilateral papers (SBIs) at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.5 percent, one- and three-month at 10.25 and 11.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 10.73 percent. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
